source_text: Sed iam apostolicae sententiae dignitas asseratur, ne putetur vel de aliquibus hoc sensisse, quod tu de omnibus aestimasti. Apostolus itaque Paulus disputans cum quaestionibus Iudaeorum, qui generis sui dignitate turgentes, dedignabantur coaequari sibi ex Gentibus fideles, et iustitiam Dei commendat et gratiam, disputans ad earum munificentiam pertinere, quod et primo Iudaeos nobilitaverat legis agnitio, et quod deinceps etiam Gentes adsciverat Christi praedicatio. Unus enim utriusque populi conditor iudicaturus et illos per legem, et istos sine lege, et istos in lege [n339] ; quia non erat Iudaeorum Deus tantum, sed etiam Gentium, reddens suum unicuique sine fraude, sine gratia [n340] , id est sine cuiusquam acceptione personae (quod exprimit nomen gratiae in definitione iustitiae), ita de semine venientes Abraham, cum nequiter vivunt, iure condemnat, ac de sua haereditate proturbat, sicut etiam Gentiles in simili operatione deprehensos; et e regione, utriusque populi bonas voluntates et veram fidem probitatemque actionum donat gaudiis sempiternis. Comprimit igitur Gentium Magister Iudaeorum tumorem, et ostendit non in seminibus humani generis, sed in moribus esse distantiam; ut se illi agnoscerent, nisi fideles esse curassent, nulla praerogativa circumcisi generis vindicandos; siquidem Iacob et Esau una seminis exceptione concepti, et una vi parientis effusi, diversos nimium exitus pro meritorum diversitate pertulerint.
pass_a_gloss: But already let the dignity of the apostolic sentence be asserted, lest it be thought that he even sensed about some this, which you estimated about all. The apostle Paul therefore disputing with the questions of the Jews, who swelling with the dignity of their own kind, were disdaining that the faithful from the Nations be made equal to themselves, both commends the justice of God and grace, disputing that it pertains to their munificence, that both first the recognition of the law had ennobled the Jews, and that thereafter also the preaching of Christ had adopted the Nations. For one founder of each people about to judge both those through the law, and these without the law, and these in the law; because he was not the God of the Jews only, but also of the Nations, returning his own to each without deceit, without favor, that is without acceptance of anyone's person (which the name of grace expresses in the definition of justice), so those coming from the seed of Abraham, when they live wickedly, he condemns by right, and drives forth from his own inheritance, as also Gentiles caught in a similar operation; and from the other side, the good wills of each people and true faith and uprightness of actions he gifts with everlasting joys. The Teacher of the Nations therefore compresses the tumor of the Jews, and shows that the distance is not in the seeds of the human race, but in manners; that those would recognize themselves, unless they had taken care to be faithful, to be vindicated by no prerogative of a circumcised kind; since indeed Jacob and Esau conceived by one taking-up of seed, and poured out by one force of the one bearing, bore too diverse exits according to the diversity of deserts.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'
LS meritum=desert; Blaise without later merit-system
LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: Let the dignity of the apostolic statement now be defended, lest it be thought that he meant about some people what you supposed about all. The apostle Paul, debating the objections of Jews who swelled with pride in the dignity of their ancestry and disdained believers from the nations being made equal to them, commends both God's justice and his grace. He argues that their generosity accounts both for the knowledge of the Law that first ennobled the Jews and for the preaching of Christ that afterward also admitted the nations. For there is one Creator of both peoples, who will judge the former through the Law, the latter without the Law, and the former in the Law (Romans 2:12; Romans 3:29–31). He is not the God of Jews alone but also of the nations (Romans 3:29), returning to each what belongs to that person without deceit or favoritism, that is, without partiality toward anyone. This is the sense of “favor” in the definition of justice (compare Romans 2:6, 11).

Thus he rightly condemns those descended from Abraham when they live wickedly and drives them from his inheritance, just as he does Gentiles found acting similarly. Conversely, he rewards the good wills, true faith, and upright deeds of either people with eternal joys. The Teacher of the Nations therefore restrains Jewish pride and shows that the difference lies not in human seed but in conduct. They must recognize that unless they take care to be faithful, no privilege of circumcised ancestry will defend them. Jacob and Esau, after all, were conceived through one reception of seed and delivered through one act of giving birth, yet experienced very different outcomes because of the difference in what they deserved (compare Genesis 25:21–26; Romans 9:10–13).

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

variants.reading: The source repeats “these” where the sequence of peoples would normally call for “those”. The translation follows the contrast between Jews judged in the Law and Gentiles without the Law, in Romans 2:12.
